**Agent M (skins): the Minecraft skin creator is built, committed and pushed, but it has never been opened in a browser.** The Playwright run never ran: it sat behind the global heavy-job lock until the stop order came, and I then cancelled it. The real Next.js render of both pages was also never done.

**Branch:** `feature/minecraft-skin-creator`, worktree `/opt/nxeon-wt-skins`. Commits `032f1e2a5b` and `9c05f4b1ff`. Progress note: `/root/agent-notes/skins.md`. Harness copy: `/root/agent-notes/skins-harness/`.

**Vetting.** "That Host" is DatHost (dathost.com/tools/minecraft-skin-editor); `that.host` is an unrelated personal domain. DatHost's editor has no licence or repo and its terms grant no reuse, so I treated it as all-rights-reserved and copied only feature ideas — no code, templates, text or branding. The verdict, feature comparison and attributions are in `docs/TOOL-SKIN-CREATOR.md`.

**What's built**
- **3D preview:** skinview3d 3.4.2 (MIT, includes three.js), vendored unmodified at `public/vendor/skinview3d-3.4.2/` with its licence texts. It loads by script tag only on the tool page, and no npm dependency was added.
  - Classic/slim models, 9 animations, orbit/zoom/pan, background and light options.
  - Per-part and per-layer visibility, cape/elytra, 3D screenshot.
  - Click a body part to jump the editor there, or paint directly on the model (hand-written picking in `components/skin-creator/sv3d.ts`).
- **2D editor:** layout guides, 9 tools, brush sizes, mirror painting, base vs overlay editing, select/move/flip/rotate/copy/paste, undo/redo, zoom/grid, keyboard shortcuts, touch with pinch zoom, palette plus recent and in-skin colours.
- **Import:** by username through `/api/tools/mc-skin` (`lib/skin/mojang.ts`):
  - fixed Mojang hosts only, and a texture-host allowlist of `textures.minecraft.net/texture/<hex>`;
  - 5s timeouts, no redirects, size caps, PNG size check;
  - in-process cache, 20 requests/min per IP plus a global ceiling.
  - PNG upload, drag-and-drop and paste also work; old 64×32 skins are converted automatically.
- **Export and templates:** PNG download, copy image, a share link that carries the PNG in the URL fragment (no new infrastructure), a Java/Bedrock how-to, and 7 original templates drawn by code.
- **Pages:** the marketing page is registered through the nxm generators (`port_pages.py tools-tool`, regenerated `live-routes.json`). JSON-LD covers SoftwareApplication, HowTo, FAQPage and breadcrumbs. The CTA points to Minecraft hosting (real "from" price) and the free Minecraft server. The portal page is `/dashboard/tools/minecraft-skin-creator` in the Nexion theme, including light mode.

**How it was checked**
- 24 unit and route tests pass: `npx tsx --test test/skin-core.test.ts test/skin-mojang.test.ts test/skin-route.test.ts`.
- The full `tsc` run showed errors only in my test typings. I fixed them, but the full re-run hasn't been done.
- I ran the nxm content loader for the new tool directly. It returns the expected copy, JSON-LD, CTA and fact chips, and the other tools come out unchanged.

**Still to do, in order**
1. Run the harness (instructions in the note). It checks drawing, mirror, undo, fill, slim/classic, overlay mode, 3D click-to-jump and paint-on-model, username import against a mocked API, legacy upload, the share link, mobile layout and screenshots. The 3D picking is the most likely thing to need fixing.
2. Render both pages on a dev server. This needs a throwaway DB with Plan/GamePlan/Node rows and a test user; I dropped mine and removed `.env`.
3. Re-run `tsc`, then `git merge main`.

**Files edited outside my area:**
- `components/marketing/ToolShell.tsx` — optional `jsonLd`/`cta`/`facts` props
- `app/nxm/_data/tools-live.ts`
- `app/nxm/_data/tools-tool.ts`
- `app/nxm/_components/ToolMount.tsx`
- `app/nxm/_seo/registry.ts`
- `app/(marketing)/tools/page.tsx`
- `lib/tools/catalog.ts`
- `app/dashboard/tools/_ToolPage.tsx` — `wide` option
- `lib/nx/icon-paths.ts`
- `lib/nx/tool-icons.ts`
- `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` — entry appended at the end, so expect merge conflicts there

No schema changes, and nothing needs the owner.

The skin creator is built, committed and pushed on `feature/minecraft-skin-creator`, but it has never been tested in a browser. The Playwright run sat behind the shared heavy-job lock until your stop order, and I then cancelled it. The 3D click-to-paint code is what I'd expect to need fixing first.

**Vetting:** "That Host" is DatHost (dathost.com/tools/minecraft-skin-editor); `that.host` itself is an unrelated personal domain. Their editor has no licence or public repo, so I copied only feature ideas — no code, templates, text or branding. The write-up is in `docs/TOOL-SKIN-CREATOR.md`.

**What's in it:**
- **3D preview:** uses skinview3d (MIT licence, includes three.js), stored as an unmodified file in the repo and loaded only on the tool page. No npm package was added.
  - Classic and slim models, 9 animations, rotate/zoom/pan, background and light options.
  - Cape support and a 3D screenshot.
  - Click a body part to jump the editor there, or paint directly on the model.
- **2D editor:** layout guides, 9 drawing tools, mirror painting, base vs overlay layers, select/move/flip/rotate, undo/redo, zoom/grid, keyboard shortcuts, touch with pinch zoom, and a palette with recent colours.
- **Import:** by Minecraft username through a new server route, `/api/tools/mc-skin`.
  - It only talks to Mojang's fixed hosts and only accepts skin images from `textures.minecraft.net`.
  - Requests have timeouts and size limits, and results are cached.
  - It allows 20 lookups a minute per visitor, plus an overall cap.
  - PNG upload, drag-and-drop and paste also work; old 64×32 skins are converted automatically.
- **Export:** PNG download, copy to clipboard, a share link with the skin inside the link itself (nothing stored on our side), and Java/Bedrock instructions. The 7 starter templates are original art drawn by code.
- **Pages:**
  - Marketing page `/tools/minecraft-skin-creator`, registered through the nxm generators, with FAQ, HowTo and SoftwareApplication structured data. Its CTA links to Minecraft hosting (with the real "from" price) and the free Minecraft server.
  - Portal page `/dashboard/tools/minecraft-skin-creator`, in the Nexion theme including light mode.

**Checked so far:**
- The new tests (24) all pass.
- The full typecheck showed errors only in my test files. I fixed those but haven't re-run it.
- I ran the new page's content loader directly: it returns the right copy, structured data and CTA, and the other tools' output is unchanged.

**Still to do:**
1. Run the browser test I wrote (saved in `/root/agent-notes/skins-harness/`). It covers drawing, mirror, undo, fill, model switch, layers, 3D click and paint, username import against a fake Mojang response, old-skin upload, the share link, mobile layout and screenshots.
2. Load both real pages on a dev server. This needs a throwaway database with plan data and a test login. I deleted mine and removed the temporary `.env` when you asked us to stop.
3. Re-run the typecheck and merge `main` into the branch.

No schema changes and nothing needs your action. To hook the tool in, I edited 10 shared files outside my area. One of them is `components/marketing/ToolShell.tsx`, which gained optional props for structured data, the CTA and the fact labels under the hero. Expect a merge conflict in `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md`, because my entry is appended at the end. The full file list, exact re-run commands and resume steps are in `/root/agent-notes/skins.md`.
